page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.1-4 is an entry-tier compute instance powered by the 64-bit Arm architecture. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs from an Ampere AmpereOne Ampere-1 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage, and operates without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest computational throughput consistent with a dual-core entry profile. Multi-core execution scores reflect the low physical core count, with a Geekbench multi-core result of 1793.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 1495.67 placing it in lower performance tiers relative to larger multi-threaded servers. Memory subsystem tests demonstrate uncached sequential reads of 13.17 GB/sec and writes of 22.96 GB/sec. Application testing shows 2.81 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and static web throughput of 3.19 GB/sec, alongside an average single-threaded gzip compression rate of 24.02 GB/sec.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is oriented toward lightweight tasks that do not demand extensive RAM pools or heavy vectorized parallelization. Because local storage is absent, instances rely on external block storage, which influences I/O predictability. Given the dedicated physical core assignment and Arm power profile, it serves as a resource-efficient environment for small background utilities, microservices, lightweight web serving, and continuous integration testing stages optimized for arm64.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.1-4 is an arm64 compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an Ampere AmpereOne Ampere-1 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. It features 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, resulting in 2 vCPUs accompanied by 4.0 GB of system memory. The instance features no local storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached block storage and provisioning one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks capture an entry-level performance tier, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1793.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1495.67, and Redis throughput of 2.81 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth yields 13.17 GB/sec for uncached reads and 22.96 GB/sec for writes. The instance provides an efficient dedicated-core footprint suitable for lightweight web serving, microservices, low-traffic API endpoints, and basic arm64 software compilation pipelines.
